title: Immunofluorescence Detection of Phosphorylated SMAD Proteins in Human Blastocysts
author: Fallesen, Brumm
materials: phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) without Ca2+ and Mg2+

steps.title: Prepare fixation and permeabilization solutions
steps.instruction: Make fresh 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) solution and use it within 7 days; store at 4 °C. Prepare a Triton‑PBS washing solution on the day of use by adding Triton X‑100 to calcium‑ and magnesium‑free PBS (no concentration specified).

substeps.instruction: Dissolve PFA to 4 % (w/v) in PBS, filter if needed, aliquot and keep at 4 °C; discard any solution older than 7 days.
Mix Triton X‑100 into PBS lacking Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ to obtain a fresh permeabilization buffer; keep on ice until use.

steps.title: Prepare glass capillary for embryo handling
steps.instruction: Fabricate a Pasteur glass capillary suitable for manual manipulation of human blastocysts, then clean and store it for reuse.

substeps.instruction: Heat a Pasteur glass pipette in a Bunsen‑burner flame.
When the glass becomes malleable, pull outward once to thin the tip.
Break off the tip so the opening is >300 µm in diameter to accommodate an expanded human blastocyst.
Briefly pass the opening through the flame to soften any sharp edges.
Inspect the opening under a stereo microscope; select capillaries with smooth, round edges and sufficient diameter.
After use, rinse sequentially with deionized water, 70 % ethanol, and acetone.
Store the capillary by adhering it to a piece of Bostik Blu‑Tack placed in a large plastic box; alternatively use a commercially available capillary of adequate diameter.

steps.title: Handle embryos and perform immunostaining
steps.instruction: All manual manipulations of human embryos are performed with a STRIPPER pipette in 4‑well dishes on a rocking platform at standard laboratory room temperature (15 °C–25 °C). Follow the immunostaining workflow described in the original publication (fixation, permeabilization, blocking, primary and secondary antibody incubations) using the solutions prepared above.

steps.title: Configure CellProfiler analysis pipeline
steps.instruction: Set up the CellProfiler modules required to segment nuclei, measure marker intensities, overlay objects, save images, and export measurements.

substeps.instruction: Load the StarDist model to segment nuclei in 2 D.
In the OverlayObjects modules, set the ‘Objects’ dropdown to “Objects_edge_size_filtered” and set Opacity to 0.3.

Configure each SaveImages module with: Image type = “Image”; file‑name method = “Sequential Numbers”; number of digits = 4; file format = TIFF; image bit depth = 8‑bit integer; lossless compression = No; output location = Default Output Folder/sub‑folder; overwrite = No; when to save = Last Cycle; record file path = No. Choose the appropriate image, prefix and sub‑folder as listed in Table 2.
Configure the ExportToSpreadsheet module: set the filename prefix as required and enable “Select the measurements to export” (set to Yes).

steps.title: Run CellProfiler on image sets
steps.instruction: Import the acquired microscopy images into CellProfiler, execute the pipeline configured above, and generate the overlay images and measurement CSV files for each embryo.

steps.title: Process CellProfiler output with Python (optional)
steps.instruction: Use the provided Jupyter notebook to convert the CellProfiler CSV files into a summary Excel workbook.

substeps.instruction: Install Python (recommended via Anaconda) and ensure Jupyter notebooks are available.
Install the required packages: run `pip install numpy pandas`.
Download the notebook “SHRUMS_Wrangling.ipynb” (or the 5‑channel version if needed).
Open the notebook in Jupyter and execute each code cell in order (use Shift‑Enter).

In the second code block, set: `input_path = '/path/to/default/Output_Folder/'`, `filename = 'Stardist_Labels_Enhanced_ImagesObjects_edge_size_filtered.csv'`, and `save_file_name = 'Date_Meaningful_Filename_All_Channels_Output.xlsx'`.
Run the remaining cells to import data, count data folders, and perform the full analysis, producing the Excel file with integrated intensities and other measurements.

steps.title: Normalize phospho‑SMAD intensity to DAPI
steps.instruction: For each tracked nucleus, divide the phospho‑SMAD fluorescence intensity by the corresponding DAPI intensity to correct for background and depth‑related variations; then manually verify nuclei with high normalized values in the original Z‑stack images.

substeps.instruction: Calculate DAPI‑normalized phospho‑SMAD intensity for every nucleus using the exported measurements.
Identify nuclei with unusually high normalized values.
Locate each such nucleus in the original microscopy Z‑frames and visually confirm true phospho‑SMAD expression.
Record validated nuclei for downstream statistical analysis.
